status.en: 23 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 26% fewer than the week before, most of them in Damascus, Quneitra and Golan Heights.
status.nb: 23 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 26 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Damaskus, Quneitra og Golanhøydene.

summary.en: Israeli forces fired across the border into southern Syria, killing a Syrian man with disabilities in the Daraa buffer zone and deploying rooftop snipers who opened fire in the south. Two Syrian security officers were killed in a raid on an ISIL cell near Damascus. Hundreds of Syrians protested repeated Israeli incursions while Syrian Christians faced heightened risk of killing or abduction. Jordanian and Syrian foreign ministers held expanded talks in Aqaba after attacks on churches in Jordan, and a US envoy noted that Syria's interim leader seeks Israel normalization. The war caused 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israelske styrker skjøt over grensen inn i Sør-Syria, og drepte en syrisk mann med funksjonsnedsettelser i Daraa-buffersonen, samt satte opp taksnikere som åpnet ild i sør. To syriske sikkerhetsoffiserer ble drept i et raid på en IS-celle nær Damaskus. Hundrevis av syrere protesterte mot gjentatte israelske inntrengninger, mens syriske kristne stod overfor økt risiko for drap eller bortføring. Jordanske og syriske utenriksministre holdt utvidede samtaler i Akaba etter angrep på kirker i Jordan, og en amerikansk sendebud bemerket at Syriens midlertidige leder søker normalisering med Israel. Krigen forårsaket 2 732 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
